claim: Heart looping is the first morphological sign of bilateral asymmetry during embryonic development.
source: Heart looping, which is the first morphological sign of bilateral asymmetry during embryonic development, is required for the correct alignment of cardiac chambers and thus for the establishment of the double blood circulation.
evidence: This is stated directly in the introduction as an established fact about heart development.

claim: Abnormal left-right patterning is associated with heterotaxy, which has an incidence of about 1/10,000.
source: Abnormal left-right patterning is associated with human diseases referred to as heterotaxy, with an incidence of about 1/10 000, including defects in the lung, spleen, liver, stomach, intestine and also complex cardiac malformations, which will determine the prognosis of patients (Lin et al., 2014; Guimier et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Lin et al., 2014 and Guimier et al., 2015.

claim: The left-right organiser, the node, is first detectable at Embryonic day (E)7.5 in the mouse.
source: The left-right organiser, the node (Nonaka et al., 1998), is first detectable in the early embryo, at Embryonic day (E)7.5 in the mouse.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Nonaka et al., 1998.

claim: Left-right patterning involves a leftward fluid flow generated by cilia.
source: Left-right patterning involves a leftward fluid flow, generated by cilia, which initiates a signalling cascade centred on the left determinant Nodal, a secretory protein of the transforming growth factor-beta (TGFβ) superfamily (Levin et al., 1995; Collignon et al., 1996; see Shiratori and Hamada, 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Levin et al., 1995, Collignon et al., 1996, and Shiratori and Hamada, 2014.

claim: In Nodal mutants, the direction of heart looping is randomised, but the process of looping still takes place.
source: For example, in Nodal mutants (Brennan et al., 2002), the direction of heart looping is randomised, but the process of looping still takes place.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Brennan et al., 2002.

claim: Formation of the cardiac tube occurs at E8 in the mouse.
source: Formation of the cardiac tube, at E8 in the mouse, is initiated on the ventral side such that the heart remains initially attached to the body dorsally, by a tissue referred to as the dorsal mesocardium, which finally breaks down at E9.5.
evidence: This is stated directly in the text as a temporal fact about mouse heart development.

claim: The dorsal mesocardium breaks down at E9.5.
source: Formation of the cardiac tube, at E8 in the mouse, is initiated on the ventral side such that the heart remains initially attached to the body dorsally, by a tissue referred to as the dorsal mesocardium, which finally breaks down at E9.5.
evidence: This is stated directly in the text as a temporal fact about mouse heart development.

claim: Growth of the myocardium inside the tube is coherent.
source: Growth of the myocardium inside the tube is coherent (Meilhac, 2003), suggesting that mixing between cells derived from the right and left heart fields is limited.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Meilhac, 2003, and leads to an inference about cell mixing.

claim: The length of the cardiac tube increases 4.4-fold between E8.5e and E8.5j.
source: We quantified the increase in the length of the cardiac tube from 183 ± 42 µm (n = 3) at E8.5e to 800 ± 56 µm (n = 3) at E8.5j (Figure 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative measurements from 3D reconstructions shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The distance between the arterial and venous poles is constant during heart looping.
source: We found that, while the length of the cardiac tube increases 4.4-fold in average between E8.5e and E8.5j, the distance between the arterial and venous poles is constant (p=0.26, Student test between E8.5e and E8.5j) with a value of 146 ± 29 µm in average (Figure 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative measurements and statistical testing shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The mouse heart tube at E8.5f is rotated towards the right side.
source: We found on HREM sections, that the mouse heart tube at E8.5f was not bilaterally symmetrical, but rather rotated towards the right side (Figure 4A–B).
evidence: This claim is supported by observations from HREM sections shown in Figure 4A-B.

claim: At E8.5f, the rotation of the arterial pole is approximately 25 degrees.
source: We estimated, at E8.5f in the mouse, that the rotation is in the order of 25° (inset Figure 4C).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative measurements shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The rotation at E8.5f is specific to the arterial pole and not significant in the venous half of the tube.
source: At E8.5f, this asymmetry was specific to the arterial pole (Student test, p<0.001) and not significant in the venous half of the tube (p>0.40).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical testing of measurements at different positions along the tube.

claim: The venous pole is significantly left-sided from E8.5g, with a minimum 47 µm ± 22 (E8.5g) and maximum 87 µm ± 10 (E8.5i) deviation.
source: We quantified the position of the venous pole of the heart relative to the notochord and found it significantly left-sided from E8.5g, with a minimum 47 µm ± 22 (E8.5g) and maximum 87 µm ± 10 (E8.5i) deviation (Figure 5A–B).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative measurements shown in Figure 5A-B.

claim: At E8.5g, there is a significant higher number of cases when right cells only had been recruited to the heart tube.
source: We evaluated whether there are instances when precursors on one side had been recruited to the heart tube and not that on the other side (Figure 5E). This was observed transiently, at stage E8.5g, with a significant higher number of cases when right cells only had been recruited to the heart tube.
evidence: This claim is supported by cell labeling experiments and quantification shown in Figure 5E.

claim: A significant increase in mitotic cells was observed in right precursors of the second heart field at E8.5g.
source: A significant increase in mitotic cells was observed in right precursors of the second heart field at E8.5g, but we did not detect any difference between the anterior and posterior domains.
evidence: This claim is supported by cell proliferation analysis shown in Figure 5F-G.

claim: The dorsal mesocardium was at least 94 ± 50 µm thick at E8.5e.
source: The dorsal mesocardium was at least 94 ± 50 µm (n = 3) thick at E8.5e and got thinner to a minimum of 28 ± 13 µm (n = 3 per stage) between E8.5f and E8.5h, corresponding to about two cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative measurements from HREM sections.

claim: Breakdown of the dorsal mesocardium was detectable from E8.5i, in the arterial half of the tube and progressed towards the venous pole at E8.5j.
source: Breakdown of the dorsal mesocardium was detectable from E8.5i, in the arterial half of the tube and progressed towards the venous pole at E8.5j (see thick lines below Figure 3D).
evidence: This claim is supported by observations from HREM sections and quantification shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Computer simulations show that two left-right asymmetries, generating opposite deformations at the poles, together with the progressive breakdown of the dorsal mesocardium, are sufficient to generate a helical shape.
source: Simulations ran with this model showed that, in the context of a tube growing between fixed poles, two left-right asymmetries, generating opposite deformations at the poles, together with the progressive breakdown of the dorsal mesocardium, were sufficient to generate a helical shape (Figure 6D), and thus a looped heart tube.
evidence: This claim is supported by computer simulations shown in Figure 6D.

claim: If the constraint of a fixed distance between the poles was released, simulations led to a C-shape heart tube.
source: If the constraint of a fixed distance between the poles was released, simulations led to a C-shape heart tube (Figure 6—figure supplement 1E), which is reminiscent of that observed in explant experiments (Manning and McLachlan, 1990).
evidence: This claim is supported by computer simulations shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1E and compared to cited experimental observations.

claim: If the dorsal mesocardium was not taken into account, simulations also produced a C-shape heart tube.
source: If the dorsal mesocardium was not taken into account, simulations also produced a C-shape heart tube (Figure 6—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This claim is supported by computer simulations shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1F.

claim: If there was no left-right asymmetry, the simulated tube remained straight in a frontal plane, with only the ventral bulge.
source: If there was no left-right asymmetry, the simulated tube remained straight in a frontal plane, with only the ventral bulge (Figure 7B abscissa = 0 and ordinate = 0).
evidence: This claim is supported by computer simulations shown in Figure 7B.

claim: If there was a single asymmetry at one pole, the simulated tube acquired a C-shape.
source: If there was a single asymmetry at one pole, again the simulated tube acquired a C-shape (Figure 7B abscissa = 0 or ordinate = 0).
evidence: This claim is supported by computer simulations shown in Figure 7B.

claim: All parameters of the model are required together for generating a helical shape.
source: This indicates that all parameters of the model are required together for generating a helical shape.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the simulation results showing that removal of any parameter leads to non-helical shapes.

claim: After 24 hr of culture from E8.5e or E8.5f, DiI label at the most cranial ventral midline was located on the right side in the looped heart.
source: To test these predictions experimentally, we injected DiI at the most cranial ventral midline, at E8.5e (Figure 8C–D) and E8.5f (Figure 8E–F), that is, before or during the stage when we first observed left-right asymmetry at the arterial pole. After 24 hr of culture, in the looped heart, the label was clearly located on the right side.
evidence: This claim is supported by cell labeling experiments shown in Figure 8C-F.

claim: Shh-/- mutant hearts fail to acquire a helical shape at a stage when control hearts are looped.
source: Reconstruction of the axis of the heart tube from HREM images showed that Shh-/- mutant hearts fail to acquire a helical shape, at a stage when control hearts are looped (Figure 9C and Figure 9—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by 3D reconstructions from HREM images shown in Figure 9C.

claim: Shh-/- mutants have a persistent dorsal mesocardium.
source: This is associated with a persistent dorsal mesocardium (Figure 9D–E and Figure 9—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by observations from HREM sections shown in Figure 9D-E and Figure 9—figure supplement 1.

claim: Between 10 and 12 somite stages, all control embryos displayed a broken down dorsal mesocardium, but this concerned only 2/5 Shh-/- mutants.
source: Between 10 and 12 somite stages, whereas all control embryos displayed a broken down dorsal mesocardium, this concerned only 2/5 mutants (Figure 9—figure supplement 1A,C).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative observations shown in Figure 9—figure supplement 1A,C.

claim: At E9.5, 2/6 Shh-/- mutants had no sign of dorsal mesocardium breakdown.
source: This was not a delay, as at E9.5, 2/6 mutants had no sign of dorsal mesocardium breakdown, and in the other 4/6 mutants, dorsal mesocardium breakdown was detected over a maximum length of 30 µm, which is much less than a breakdown over a minimum of 124 µm in control littermates (Figure 9—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative observations shown in Figure 9—figure supplement 2.

claim: The direction of the loop in Shh-/- mutants was found normally rightward (n = 5/5 at E8.5, 6/6 at E9.5).
source: The direction of the loop was found normally rightward (n = 5/5 at E8.5, 6/6 at E9.5) (Figure 9—source data 1 and Figure 9—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by observations from multiple mutant embryos.

claim: Shh-/- mutants have a significantly shorter heart tube compared to control samples.
source: When we measured the tube length, we found that Shh-/- mutants have a significantly shorter heart tube, compared to control samples (Figure 9G).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative measurements shown in Figure 9G.

claim: Shh-/- mutants have a significant 1.2-fold increase in tube perimeter compared to controls.
source: Thus, we measured the perimeter of the heart tube in Shh-/- mutants and found a significant 1.2-fold increase compared to controls (Figure 9H, Student test, p=0.03).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative measurements and statistical testing shown in Figure 9H.

claim: The overall area of the heart tube did not change significantly between Shh-/- mutants and controls.
source: The overall area of the heart tube did not change significantly between mutants and controls (0.56 ± 0.12 mm2 and 0.55 ± 1.0 mm2, respectively, n = 5 and 5, Student test, p=0.75), further showing that there is no overall growth defects in Shh-/- mutant hearts.
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative measurements and statistical testing.

claim: The distance between the poles is not significantly changed in Shh-/- mutant hearts.
source: We also confirmed that the distance between the poles is not significantly changed in Shh-/- mutant hearts (121 ± 15 µm, compared to 132 ± 17 µm in controls, n = 5 and 5, p=0.31, Student test).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative measurements and statistical testing.

claim: Shh-/- mutant hearts have a narrower curvature of the tube axis in the transverse plane compared to controls.
source: Finally, computer simulations predict that persistence of the dorsal mesocardium constrains the curvature of the tube axis in the transverse plane. This prediction is validated in Shh-/- mutant hearts, in which we observed a narrower curvature of the tube axis in the transverse plane (Figure 9H–J).
evidence: This claim is supported by computer simulations and quantitative measurements shown in Figure 9H-J.

claim: There is a good match between the shape of Shh-/- mutant hearts and the simulated shape in case of persistent dorsal mesocardium, both qualitatively and quantitatively for four geometrical parameters.
source: In summary, there is a discrepancy between the real shape of Shh-/- mutant hearts and the simulated shape in case of reduced left-right signalling. In contrast, there is a good match between the shape of Shh-/- mutant hearts and the simulated shape in case of persistent dorsal mesocardium, both qualitatively and quantitatively for the change of values of four geometrical parameters.
evidence: This claim is supported by comparison of simulation results with experimental observations shown in Figure 9H.

claim: Mmp2 is expressed in the foregut of the mouse at the beginning of heart looping (E8.5g), with vesicular localisations in the cardiac region.
source: We detected expression of Mmp2 in the foregut of the mouse at the beginning of heart looping (E8.5g), with vesicular localisations in the cardiac region, suggesting secretion of Mmp2 (Figure 10A).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunostaining shown in Figure 10A.

claim: Upon GM6001 treatment, all control embryos (3/3) displayed a broken down dorsal mesocardium, but this concerned only 2/4 treated embryos.
source: After 10 hr of culture, the embryos reached stage E8.5h-i in the control situation (DMSO) (Figure 10C). Whereas all control embryos (3/3) displayed a broken down dorsal mesocardium, this concerned only 2/4 mutants (Figure 10D–E).
evidence: This claim is supported by observations from embryo culture experiments shown in Figure 10C-E.

claim: After 24 hr of GM6001 treatment, the right ventricle failed in most cases (7/9) to reach a right position relative to the left ventricle.
source: After 24 hr of culture, the right ventricle failed in most cases (7/9) to reach a right position relative to the left ventricle (Figure 10F), leading to a tube shape similar to that predicted by the computer model (Figure 9A).
evidence: This claim is supported by observations from embryo culture experiments shown in Figure 10F.

claim: The buckling mechanism is able to generate asymmetric morphogenesis by amplifying small left-right variations.
source: The buckling mechanism is thus able to generate asymmetric morphogenesis by amplifying small left-right variations.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from computer simulations showing that small asymmetries lead to curved tubes.

claim: A buckling mechanism is insufficient to account for the biological helical shape of the looped heart tube.
source: However, in this minimal hypothesis, the tube acquired a C-shape. Therefore, a buckling mechanism is insufficient to account for the biological helical shape of the looped heart tube.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from computer simulations showing that buckling alone produces C-shapes, not helices.

claim: The model provides a novel predictive model of heart looping based on the buckling of the tube when growing between fixed poles.
source: Thus, we provide a novel predictive model of heart looping, based on the buckling of the tube, when growing between fixed poles. Buckling is modulated by the progressive breakdown of the dorsal mesocardium and biased by a precise combination of left-right asymmetries at the poles, thus generating a helical shape.
evidence: This is a summary claim synthesizing the results of the study.

claim: The parameter space of left-right asymmetries compatible with the helix shape observed in vivo is narrow.
source: The parameter space of left-right asymmetries compatible with the helix shape observed in vivo is narrow.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from exploration of parameter space in computer simulations shown in Figure 7.

claim: A tight coordination between the intensities and positions of left-right asymmetry at either pole is required for generating a helical shape.
source: A tight coordination between the intensities and positions of left-right asymmetry at either pole is required.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from exploration of parameter space in computer simulations shown in Figure 7.

claim: The model functions as a generator of asymmetric morphogenesis, able to amplify initial left-right differences between heart precursors.
source: Our predictive model is validated in four experimental conditions, using cell labelling, time-lapse imaging and molecular deficiencies. The novel model of heart looping that we propose functions as a generator of asymmetric organ morphogenesis, in the sense of Brown and Wolpert(1990), able to amplify initial left-right differences between heart precursors.
evidence: This is a synthesis claim drawing on the overall results and citing Brown and Wolpert (1990) for the concept of a generator of asymmetric morphogenesis.

claim: Heart looping is required for the correct alignment of cardiac chambers and establishment of double blood circulation.
source: Heart looping, which is the first morphological sign of bilateral asymmetry during embryonic development, is required for the correct alignment of cardiac chambers and thus for the establishment of the double blood circulation.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about the functional importance of heart looping.

claim: The cardiac tube undergoes a process of rightward looping.
source: In the case of the heart, the primordium is a tube, which undergoes a process of rightward looping (Patten, 1922), thereby acquiring a helical shape (Männer, 2004; see Männer, 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Patten, 1922, Männer, 2004, and Männer, 2009.

claim: The cardiac tube acquires a helical shape during looping.
source: In the case of the heart, the primordium is a tube, which undergoes a process of rightward looping (Patten, 1922), thereby acquiring a helical shape (Männer, 2004; see Männer, 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Männer, 2004 and Männer, 2009.

claim: Formation of the cardiac tube occurs by fusion of two bilateral heart fields.
source: Formation of the cardiac tube occurs under the head folds, by fusion of two bilateral heart fields (Rawles and Rawles, 1943; Kinder et al., 1999).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Rawles and Rawles, 1943 and Kinder et al., 1999.

claim: Heart precursors are detected in two waves, referred to as the first and second heart fields.
source: Heart precursors are detected in two waves, referred to as the first and second heart fields (see Meilhac et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Meilhac et al., 2014.

claim: Elongation of the heart tube progresses cranially and caudally by ingression of heart precursors.
source: Elongation of the heart tube progresses cranially and caudally by ingression of heart precursors (Stalsberg, 1969; de la Cruz et al., 1977) and also by proliferation of cells inside the tube (de Boer et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Stalsberg, 1969 and de la Cruz et al., 1977.

claim: Elongation of the heart tube also occurs by proliferation of cells inside the tube.
source: Elongation of the heart tube progresses cranially and caudally by ingression of heart precursors (Stalsberg, 1969; de la Cruz et al., 1977) and also by proliferation of cells inside the tube (de Boer et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to de Boer et al., 2012.

claim: Left and right heart precursors contribute to specific regions of the mouse heart tube.
source: In agreement with this, cell-labelling experiments have shown that left and right heart precursors contribute to specific regions of the mouse heart tube (Domínguez et al., 2012) and later, in the fetal heart, to specific veins, atrial regions or specific great arteries (Lescroart et al., 2010; Lescroart et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Domínguez et al., 2012, Lescroart et al., 2010, and Lescroart et al., 2012.

claim: Looping of the tube is concomitant with elongation.
source: Looping of the tube is concomitant with elongation (Biben and Harvey, 1997), raising the possibility that the two processes may be linked.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Biben and Harvey, 1997 and leads to speculation about linkage.

claim: Early embryologists observed that the elongation of the heart tube is constrained.
source: In the context of the heart, looping mechanisms have been mainly studied in the chick. Early embryologists made the morphological observation that the elongation of the heart tube is constrained (His, 1868).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to His, 1868.

claim: The increase of the tube length is much greater than that of the distance between the attached cranial and caudal ends.
source: Measurements indicated that the increase of the tube length is much greater than that of the distance between the attached cranial (arterial) and caudal (venous) ends (Patten, 1922), leading to the proposal that looping results from a buckling mechanism, when the tube elongates between fixed poles.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Patten, 1922.

claim: Explant experiments showed curvature of isolated heart tubes.
source: This mechanism was challenged by explant experiments, showing curvature of isolated heart tubes (Manning and McLachlan, 1990), thus pointing to intrinsic rather than extrinsic factors for heart looping.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Manning and McLachlan, 1990.

claim: Surgical disconnection of the arterial pole impaired heart looping.
source: In addition, surgical disconnection of a single pole (the arterial pole) impaired heart looping (Kidokoro et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Kidokoro et al., 2008.

claim: Increased growth in the left atrial region can bias the direction of heart looping and generate a rightward C-shape.
source: Simulations with a Finite Element Analysis model, in combination with experiments in the chick, have shown how intrinsic and local variations in tissue stiffness or growth can influence phases of heart looping: the increase in cell size ventrally can generate the initial ventral bulge of the heart tube (Soufan et al., 2006; Shi et al., 2014a), whereas increased growth in the left atrial region can bias the direction of heart looping and generate a rightward C-shape (Kidokoro et al., 2008; Shi et al., 2014b; Voronov et al., 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Kidokoro et al., 2008, Shi et al., 2014b, and Voronov et al., 2004.

claim: Nodal is transiently expressed in heart precursors and turned off within the heart tube.
source: Whether intrinsic factors are dependent on the Nodal left-right signalling cascade remains undetermined, since Nodal is transiently expressed in heart precursors and turned off within the heart tube (Vincent et al., 2004), and since the Nodal target Pitx2c, which is expressed in the heart tube, is not required for heart looping (Lu et al., 1999).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Vincent et al., 2004.

claim: The Nodal target Pitx2c is not required for heart looping.
source: Whether intrinsic factors are dependent on the Nodal left-right signalling cascade remains undetermined, since Nodal is transiently expressed in heart precursors and turned off within the heart tube (Vincent et al., 2004), and since the Nodal target Pitx2c, which is expressed in the heart tube, is not required for heart looping (Lu et al., 1999).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Lu et al., 1999.

claim: Removal of the pericardial membrane does not impair heart looping in the longer term.
source: However, removal of the pericardial membrane does not impair heart looping in the longer term (Kidokoro et al., 2008; Nerurkar et al., 2006), questioning the role of this confinement.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Kidokoro et al., 2008 and Nerurkar et al., 2006.

claim: Failure of the dorsal mesocardium to break down has been associated with incomplete heart looping in Shh-/- mouse mutants.
source: Yet, failure of the dorsal mesocardium to break down has been associated with incomplete heart looping, for example in Shh-/- mouse mutants (Hildreth et al., 2009) or upon inhibition of matrix metalloproteinases in the chick (Linask et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Hildreth et al., 2009 and Linask et al., 2005.

claim: Left-right asymmetries of the dorsal mesocardium have been reported.
source: Left-right asymmetries of the dorsal mesocardium have also been reported (Linask et al., 2003; Linask et al., 2005), further pointing to this structure as a potential factor of heart looping.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Linask et al., 2003 and Linask et al., 2005.

claim: The dorsal mesentery is involved in the looping of the gut as a result of left-right asymmetries in its cellular architecture.
source: A structure analogous to the dorsal mesocardium of the heart tube, the dorsal mesentery, has been shown to be involved in the looping of another tube, the gut, as a result of left-right asymmetries in its cellular architecture (Davis et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Davis et al., 2008.

claim: The staging system proposed extends that proposed previously by Biben and Harvey, 1997.
source: Our staging system extends that proposed previously (Biben and Harvey, 1997).
evidence: This is a direct statement comparing the current staging system to a previous one.

claim: The distance between the poles of the chick heart tube is 600-800 µm.
source: The distance between the poles of the chick heart tube has long been reported to be fixed (Patten, 1922). However, the value is higher in the chick (600–800 µm) compared to the mouse (100–200 µm), and thus, a straight heart tube is more obvious in the chick.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Patten, 1922 and comparison with mouse measurements.

claim: A rightward rotation of the ventricular region in the chick was shown by labelling with iron oxide particles.
source: A rightward rotation of the ventricular region in the chick was shown by labelling with iron oxide particles (de la Cruz et al., 1977; de la Cruz, 1998), preceding the leftward displacement of the venous pole (Kidokoro et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to de la Cruz et al., 1977, de la Cruz, 1998, and Kidokoro et al., 2008.

claim: An asymmetric ingression of heart precursors, in favour of right cells, has been observed in the chick by grafting experiments at the beginning of heart looping.
source: An asymmetric ingression of heart precursors, in favour of right cells, has also been observed in the chick by grafting experiments at the beginning of heart looping (HH10, Stalsberg, 1969).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Stalsberg, 1969.

claim: In the zebrafish, formation of the heart tube involves the formation of a cone, which telescopes out to form a tube.
source: In the zebrafish, formation of the heart tube follows a different morphogenetic process, involving the formation of a cone, which telescopes out to form a tube (Stainier et al., 1993).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Stainier et al., 1993.

claim: The looped heart tube in the zebrafish is a flat-S, distinct from the helix in chick and mouse.
source: The looped heart tube in the zebrafish is a flat-S, distinct from the helix in chick and mouse.
evidence: This is stated as a comparative observation about heart tube shapes across species.

claim: Looping in zebrafish was shown to depend on intrinsic factors.
source: The fish tube does not grow between fixed poles, has no equivalent of the dorsal mesocardium, and looping was shown to depend on intrinsic factors (Noël et al., 2013), thus ruling out a buckling mechanism.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Noël et al., 2013.

claim: Left-right asymmetry of the zebrafish heart tube is first seen at the venous pole, with a leftward displacement of the atrial region referred to as cardiac jogging.
source: However, left-right asymmetry of the zebrafish heart tube is first seen at the venous pole, with a leftward displacement of the atrial region referred to as cardiac jogging (Chen et al., 1997), resulting from asymmetric migration and involution of cells in the cardiac cone (Baker et al., 2008; Rohr et al., 2008; Smith et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Chen et al., 1997, Baker et al., 2008, Rohr et al., 2008, and Smith et al., 2008.

claim: Left-right asymmetric cell proliferation, in favour of right cells and depending on the Nodal target Pitx2c, has been observed in the sinus venosus of the mouse at the seven somite stage.
source: Left-right asymmetric cell proliferation, in favour of right cells and depending on the Nodal target Pitx2c, has been observed in the sinus venosus of the mouse at the seven somite stage (Galli et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Galli et al., 2008.

claim: Breakdown of the dorsal mesocardium in the chick is not associated with apoptosis, but depends on the activity of matrix metalloproteinases.
source: Breakdown of the dorsal mesocardium was shown, in the chick, not to be associated with apoptosis, but rather to depend on the activity of matrix metalloproteinases (Linask et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Linask et al., 2005.

claim: Regionalisation of the second heart field into anterior and posterior domains has been characterised at E9.5 based on epithelial markers and differential gene expression.
source: Such regionalisation has been characterised later, at E9.5, based on epithelial markers (Francou et al., 2014) and differential gene expression, for example of the transcription factors Tbx1 and Tbx5, respectively (Rana et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Francou et al., 2014 and Rana et al., 2014.

claim: Hh signalling is required in the lateral plate mesoderm for the establishment of left-right patterning.
source: Hh signalling was shown to be required in the lateral plate mesoderm for the establishment of left-right patterning. However, in this context, Shh and Ihh ligands are redundant, so that it is only in the double mutant of the ligands (Shhflox/-; Ihhflox/-; Sox2-Cre) or in the mutant of the receptor (Smo-/-) that left markers are absent in the lateral plate mesoderm (Tsiairis and McMahon, 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Tsiairis and McMahon, 2009.

claim: Shh is required for the formation of the floorplate, which functions as a barrier for the maintenance of left-right asymmetry.
source: Shh is also required for the formation of the floorplate, which functions as a barrier for the maintenance of left-right asymmetry (Meyers and Martin, 1999).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Meyers and Martin, 1999.

claim: In Shh-/- mutants, Nodal expression is initiated correctly, whereas the downstream target Pitx2 is bilaterally expressed.
source: In Shh-/- mutants, Nodal expression is initiated correctly, whereas the downstream target Pitx2 is bilaterally expressed (Hildreth et al., 2009; Meyers and Martin, 1999).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Hildreth et al., 2009 and Meyers and Martin, 1999.

claim: Shh has been shown to regulate cell differentiation in the second heart field.
source: Shh has been shown to regulate cell differentiation in the second heart field (Goddeeris et al., 2008; Zhang et al., 2001), thus affecting the growth of the heart.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Goddeeris et al., 2008 and Zhang et al., 2001.

claim: The importance of growth of the cardiac tube as a pre-requisite for buckling is supported by looping defects in mouse mutants with reduced ingression of heart progenitors.
source: The importance of growth of the cardiac tube, as a pre-requisite for the buckling, is supported experimentally by the looping defects observed in mouse mutants with reduced ingression of heart progenitors, when the cardiomyocyte differentiation cascade is affected (see mutants for Nkx2-5 [Lyons et al., 1995], Mef2c [Lin et al., 1997], Isl1 [Cai et al., 2003], Tbx20 [Stennard et al., 2005] or Tbx3 [Ribeiro et al., 2007]).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to multiple mutant studies: Lyons et al., 1995, Lin et al., 1997, Cai et al., 2003, Stennard et al., 2005, and Ribeiro et al., 2007.

claim: Expression of Nodal is detected in heart precursors, and not within the heart tube.
source: Expression of the major left determinant Nodal is detected in heart precursors, and not within the heart tube (Collignon et al., 1996; Vincent et al., 2004), whereas the Nodal target Pitx2c, which is expressed in the heart tube, is not required for heart looping (Lu et al., 1999).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Collignon et al., 1996 and Vincent et al., 2004.

claim: In the absence or in case of bilateral expression of Nodal, the process of asymmetric morphogenesis still takes place with random orientation.
source: This elegant model of left-right patterning is supported by the observation that in the absence (Brennan et al., 2002) or in case of bilateral expression (Murray and Gridley, 2006) of the left determinant Nodal, the process of asymmetric morphogenesis still takes place, that is, the heart does not remain symmetrical and some heart looping occurs, with a random orientation, probably due to stochastic and spontaneous left-right variations.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Brennan et al., 2002 and Murray and Gridley, 2006.

claim: The model predicts that very small localised differences in growth rate (in the order of 1%) will lead to significant buckling.
source: Simulations with our model (Figure 6) predict that very small localised differences in growth rate (in the order of 1%) will lead to significant buckling.
evidence: This is a prediction from computer simulations shown in Figure 6.

claim: The curvature is stronger with a progressive breakdown of a dorsal attachment than without.
source: The curvature is stronger with a progressive breakdown of a dorsal attachment than without (data not shown).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from simulations, though the data is not shown.

claim: Left-right cellular asymmetries in the dorsal mesentery are sufficient to generate a leftward tilt of the gut.
source: Left-right cellular asymmetries in the dorsal mesentery have been uncovered, with elegant cell-based computer simulations showing that this is sufficient to generate a leftward tilt of the gut.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from previous work on gut looping, though no specific citation is provided in this sentence.

claim: The model at the tissue level will be useful to predict which tubular shape emerges from a given combination of mechanical constraints and left-right asymmetries.
source: Our model at the tissue level will be generally useful to predict which tubular shape emerges from a given combination of mechanical constraints and left-right asymmetries.
evidence: This is a prospective claim about the utility of the model.
